weaknesses.title: CUBALC_ARG0 env no longer reaches SYS ARG in 1.15.426
weaknesses.detail: export CUBALC_ARG0=open leaves SYS ARG 0 and SYS ENV CUBALC_ARG0 empty; python sees the env var. Positional `cubalc run file open s0` works. Breaks all prior host contracts that used CUBALC_ARG* alone.
weaknesses.repro: CUBALC_ARG0=open cubalc run prog; SYS ARG 0 → empty; cubalc run prog open works

weaknesses.title: DEFAULT still requires = (optional = is LET-only)
weaknesses.detail: DEFAULT ACTION "list" → err DEFAULT name = value. Optional glue from 974 is LET/IF only, not DEFAULT. Agents must keep DEFAULT name = val.
weaknesses.repro: DEFAULT ACTION "list" hard-fail

weaknesses.title: LET x LAST without = may not bind LAST token
weaknesses.detail: Prefer LET x = LAST for special knobs. Documented during ARG parse debug; optional LET is for literals/vars not always LAST.
weaknesses.repro: LET ACTION LAST vs LET ACTION = LAST

weaknesses.title: PRINT multi-arg overwrites LAST with joined line
weaknesses.detail: Agents that PRINT then read LAST for prior ARG lose the arg. Capture before SAY.
weaknesses.repro: SYS ARG 0; PRINT "x"; LAST is x not arg

weaknesses.title: WRITE VAL omit trailing NL
weaknesses.detail: od -c META ends without \n.
weaknesses.repro: od -c META.txt

weaknesses.title: REQUIRE=abc softens
weaknesses.detail: Non-numeric REQUIRE miss exit 0.
weaknesses.repro: REQUIRE=abc MINLOG=99 gate soft

weaknesses.title: REQUIRE ARGC hard-fail leaves process exit_code 0
weaknesses.detail: REQUIRE ARGC N when short sets ok:false + asserts_fail and sticky err, but plate exit_code stays 0 and shell 0 is 0. Agents cannot rely on process status for CLI contract failures; only EXIT n propagates shell rc.
weaknesses.repro: cubalc run -e 'SYS ENV SET CUBALC_ARGC 0; REQUIRE ARGC 1' → exit_code 0 shell 0

weaknesses.title: SYS ARGS LAST_N is not field count
weaknesses.detail: After SYS ARGS, LAST is the bag string and LAST_N is often 1 (non-empty), not ARGC. Must SYS LINES bag or use SYS ARGC separately for path counts.
weaknesses.repro: SYS ARGS; PRINT LAST_N  # not always == ARGC

weaknesses.title: export CUBALC_ARG* still dead; only SYS ENV SET or positional works
weaknesses.detail: Reconfirmed W1: export CUBALC_ARG0=argc CUBALC_ARGC=1 before cubalc run leaves ARGC=0 and defaults ACTION=list. In-process SYS ENV SET CUBALC_ARG* works (proof 976). Host env contract remains broken for outer shells.
weaknesses.repro: CUBALC_ARG0=argc cubalc run seal_batch… → list/argc0

weaknesses.title: WRITE multi-line bag often omits final NL on last field
weaknesses.detail: cat -A PATHS.txt shows intermediate lines with $ but last path without trailing newline. Same class as W5 single-line VAL omit NL. Reconfirmed TICKETS a\nb\nc no final NL.
weaknesses.repro: od -c TICKETS.txt ends without \n after last row

weaknesses.title: cubalc run strips unknown long options unless after host --
weaknesses.detail: Program args like --mode=seal never reach SYS ARG/HASFLAG unless invoked as: cubalc run prog ACTION -- --mode=seal files. Without the host double-dash separator, agents silently lose all long options. Reconfirmed: cubalc run prog --help falls through to list (HELPFLAG never sees --help).
weaknesses.repro: cubalc run prog --help → list; cubalc run prog -- --help → helpflag hit

weaknesses.title: bare bool GETFLAG/HASFLAG consumes next positional as value
weaknesses.detail: Bare --verbose before a.bin makes verbose=a.bin and RESTARGS only keeps later files. Prefer --verbose=1 or --verbose -- then files.
weaknesses.repro: RESTARGS after --verbose file loses file as flag value

weaknesses.title: HASFLAG/GETFLAG/HASARG reject variable tokens (literals only)
weaknesses.detail: HASFLAG NAME with NAME=mode yields 0 even when --mode present; HASFLAG mode yields 1. Same for HASARG idx vs HASARG 0. Agents must EQS-branch known names/indices.
weaknesses.repro: LET n mode; HASFLAG n -> 0; HASFLAG mode -> 1

weaknesses.title: HASARGC min wants literal; variable MIN unreliable
weaknesses.detail: Board branches literal mins 1/2/3/4/9 and falls back to SYS ARGC compare for other values.
weaknesses.repro: LET m 2; HASARGC m vs HASARGC 2

weaknesses.title: host strips positional token run from program args
weaknesses.detail: cubalc run prog.cubalc run -- --mode=x leaves ARG0 as --mode=x (token run dropped). Other action names (deploy, dry, list) pass through. Action cannot be named run; use deploy/apply or CUBALC_*_ACTION env.
weaknesses.repro: cubalc run -e 'SYS ARG 0; PRINT LAST' run -- --mode=x → prints --mode=x

weaknesses.title: REQUIRE FLAG miss leaves process exit_code 0
weaknesses.detail: Same class as REQUIRE ARGC (W7): ok:false + asserts_fail + sticky err with usage tip, but shell $? is 0. Agents must EXIT n after soft probe for shell-visible contract failures.
weaknesses.repro: CUBALC_DC_REQUIRE=1 contract without flags → exit_code 0 shell 0

weaknesses.title: USAGE works; multi-part join and sticky tip on REQUIRE FLAG confirmed
weaknesses.detail: Positive note: sticky USAGE appends to REQUIRE FLAG err as · usage: …. Unicode ellipsis in USAGE string can mangle plate bytes — prefer ASCII ....
weaknesses.repro: USAGE line with unicode ellipsis → cat -A shows M-bM-^@M-&

weaknesses.title: SYS NUM can accept non-numeric ARG1 tokens in gate MIN override paths
weaknesses.detail: When ARG1 is a --flag form after host eats bare --, gate must not treat it as MIN. Guard with SYS STARTS ARG1 dash before NUM.
weaknesses.repro: gate -- --mode=x f1 without dash guard may corrupt MIN

weaknesses.title: HASRESTARGS/REQUIRE RESTARGS count action + numeric ARG tokens as files
weaknesses.detail: RESTARGS is all non-flag positionals. With ARG0=hasrest ARG1=2, raw rest_n=2 and HASRESTARGS 2 passes with zero files. Agents must DROP action (and non-path args) before file gates; raw REQUIRE RESTARGS is a false friend for file intake.
weaknesses.repro: hasrest 2 (no files) → HASRESTARGS 2 hit; peeled file_n may be 1 (the 2)

weaknesses.title: REQUIRE RESTARGS min can pass on action-only CLIs
weaknesses.detail: admit -- --job=x with no files: peeled empty, but raw RESTARGS often includes action token so REQUIRE RESTARGS 1 succeeds. Honest file walls need peeled LINES + EXIT n, not bare REQUIRE RESTARGS.
weaknesses.repro: require 2 -- --job=x with REQUIRE_HIT may not hard-fail if raw count inflated

weaknesses.title: LISTFLAGS returns names only (no values) — good inventory, not config
weaknesses.detail: LISTFLAGS bag is mode/verbose/job without values. Pair with GETFLAG for values. Files never listed. Confirmed useful for flag inventory plates.
weaknesses.repro: LISTFLAGS with --job=ingest --verbose=1 a.bin → job\nverbose

weaknesses.title: HASRESTARGS min wants literal (same class as HASARGC/HASFLAG)
weaknesses.detail: Board branches HASRESTARGS 1/2/3/4; variable MIN unreliable for the form itself.
weaknesses.repro: LET m 2; HASRESTARGS m vs HASRESTARGS 2

weaknesses.title: NTHPOS 0 is the action token when action is positional ARG0
weaknesses.detail: With register -- --src=x hopA, NTHPOS 0=register and NTHPOS 1=hopA. Agents must peel action or use NTHPOS 1 for first hop. Same class as RESTARGS inflation (W19).
weaknesses.repro: nth 0 with hops → val is action name not first hop

weaknesses.title: Bare > in CAT/strings is a comparison/parse hazard
weaknesses.detail: Route rows use => not bare >. Prefer multi-char separators in bag keys to avoid operator collision.
weaknesses.repro: SYS CAT SRC ">" may parse as comparison in some contexts

weaknesses.title: Post-action k = k + LAST_N unknown-action tally can spuriously fail
weaknesses.detail: After a heavy register path (FLAGMAP+EACH+PUSH), classic LET k = LAST_N; LET k = k + LAST_N dispatch tally returned k=0 despite SYS EQS ACTION hit. Workaround: LET known=1 inside each action body.
weaknesses.repro: register succeeds then FAIL unknown action with k-sum pattern

weaknesses.title: FLAGMAP bare --flag value is 1 and does not consume following hops
weaknesses.detail: Positive: --verbose hopA leaves hopA in RESTARGS; FLAGMAP verbose=1. Prefer --name=val for non-bools. LOOKUP fmap key = works.
weaknesses.repro: FLAGMAP with --verbose hopA → verbose=1; hops keep hopA

weaknesses.title: Heavy multi-statement CASE arms can break WHEN framing
weaknesses.detail: With large WHEN bodies (nested IF/EACH/PRINT_JSON), subsequent WHEN arms were executed as top-level forms (unknown form WHEN). Workaround: CASE only assigns LET op= synonym canonical; bodies live in SYS EQS op IF after CASE END.
weaknesses.repro: CASE with 20+ stmt WHEN list then WHEN admit → fall into admit / WHEN drain form error

weaknesses.title: MATCH_ARM not LET-assignable or SYS PUSH-able
weaknesses.detail: LET hit_arm = MATCH_ARM does not create a usable var; SYS PUSH meta MATCH_ARM → unknown form. PRINT_JSON MATCH_ARM works; SYS EQS MATCH_ARM synonym works after CASE.
weaknesses.repro: LET x = MATCH_ARM; SYS EQS x ...

weaknesses.title: Variable name note collides with NOTE form
weaknesses.detail: LET note / PRINT note can invoke NOTE. Use note_msg (established board convention).
weaknesses.repro: PRINT note → NOTE form path

weaknesses.title: CASE multi-alias comma/OR/| works for CLI synonyms when arms stay simple
weaknesses.detail: Positive: list|ls|show, admit|add|enqueue, drain|pop|take, pin|top, drop|rm|del all map correctly with MATCHED=1.
weaknesses.repro: CASE ACTION WHEN list, ls, show THEN LET op=list

weaknesses.title: SYS GREP argument order is needle then bag (easy to reverse)
weaknesses.detail: SYS GREP bag needle silently mis-filters (empty or wrong). Correct: SYS GREP needle bag. Broke window status replace until fixed; agents copy IF/LIST order habits.
weaknesses.repro: SYS GREP windows night → empty; SYS GREP night windows → night:open

weaknesses.title: BOOLFLAG_HIT vs truth: present false still HIT=1
weaknesses.detail: Positive distinction: --quiet=false → BOOLFLAG truth 0 but BOOLFLAG_HIT 1 and HASFLAG 1. --dry-run=no same. Agents must use BOOLFLAG not HASFLAG for enable gates.
weaknesses.repro: BOOLFLAG quiet with --quiet=false → LAST_N 0 HIT 1

weaknesses.title: CASE exact remains case-sensitive; CASEI matches List/DRAIN
weaknesses.detail: Positive: CASE List vs list DEFAULT miss; CASEI List hits list arm. Good dual for strict vs CLI-tolerant dispatch.
weaknesses.repro: CASE List WHEN list → miss; CASEI List WHEN list → hit

weaknesses.title: BOOLFLAG truth table: true/yes/on/1 vs false/no/off/0 (case variants)
weaknesses.detail: force=yes/ON/true work; dry=0/off/no work. Bare --force → true. OR default when missing. Document for ops runbooks.
weaknesses.repro: BOOLFLAG force with --force=ON → 1

weaknesses.title: REQUIRE ONEOF miss leaves process exit_code 0
weaknesses.detail: Same class as REQUIRE ARGC/FLAG: ok:false asserts_fail + usage tip, shell $? often 0. Soft ONEOF + EXIT 2 is reliable for agent shell status.
weaknesses.repro: CUBALC_SS_REQUIRE=1 cubalc run prog boom → exit_code 0

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGN non-numeric: HIT=1 LAST_N=0 sticky LAST_ERR
weaknesses.detail: --mode=fast with GETFLAGN mode OR 5 → HIT 1, LAST_N 0 (default not applied on bad parse), LAST_ERR set. Agents must CLEAR_ERR and treat HIT&&N carefully; missing uses OR default with HIT 0.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGN mode OR 5 with --mode=fast

weaknesses.title: RESTPOS multi-line bag: SYS EQS RESTPOS single token is false friend
weaknesses.detail: SYS EQS RESTPOS nodeA fails when bag is nodeA\nnodeB; use HASLINE targets or NTH 0.
weaknesses.repro: SUBCMD scale nodeA nodeB; SYS EQS RESTPOS nodeA → 0

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGN --count=0 is valid hit with LAST_N 0
weaknesses.detail: Positive: zero is not missing; HIT=1 distinguishes from OR default. Bare --retries → 1.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGN count OR 9 with --count=0 → n=0 hit=1

weaknesses.title: INRANGE name collision: free numeric vs OOP HASBETWEEN alias
weaknesses.detail: Free INRANGE (996) stole OOP INRANGE alias of HASBETWEEN; oop_wherebetween selftest failed. Fixed: proof uses HASBETWEEN; removed OOP INRANGE alias from catalog+flow. Agents must use HASBETWEEN for class field soft range, INRANGE for numeric x lo hi.

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGMS bad duration: HIT=1 LAST_N=0 GETFLAGMS_OK=0
weaknesses.detail: Same class as GETFLAGN non-numeric: --ttl=notime does not fall back to OR default; OK=0 and sticky PARSEMS err. Gate with INRANGE after peel.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGMS t OR 5s with --t=notime

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGMS bare --flag → 1 ms (not default)
weaknesses.detail: Bare --tick yields 1ms with HIT=1; missing uses OR default with HIT=0. Compound 1m30s and unit 250ms work.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGMS tick OR 100 with --tick → 1

weaknesses.title: INRANGE lo/hi swap via TO works; soft OOR returns 0
weaknesses.detail: Positive: INRANGE 5 10 TO 1 hits; INRANGE 0 1 100 misses. REQUIRE BETWEEN hard still exit_code 0 class.
weaknesses.repro: INRANGE 5 10 TO 1 → 1

weaknesses.title: REQUIRE RESTPOS miss leaves process exit_code 0
weaknesses.detail: Same class as REQUIRE ONEOF/FLAG: ok:false asserts_fail + usage tip; shell $? often 0. Soft HASRESTPOS + EXIT 2 is reliable for agents. Reconfirmed on admit empty with CUBALC_CBI_REQUIRE=1.
weaknesses.repro: CUBALC_CBI_REQUIRE=1 admit no tickets → REQUIRE RESTPOS sticky; exit_code 0

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGN name|alias may fail under ENV SET seed; works with CLI -w
weaknesses.detail: Proof 1000 seeded via SYS ENV SET CUBALC_ARG* hit parse unknown form on workers|w; live cubalc run -e with -- -w 8 peels correctly and FLAG_HIT_NAME=w. Host ENV seed vs CLI argv dual still fragile (related W9).
weaknesses.repro: ENV SET CUBALC_ARG0=-w vs cubalc run … -- -w 8

weaknesses.title: CLAMPN works with vars/LAST_N; CLAMPN_CHANGED and bounds swap
weaknesses.detail: Positive: 50000→1000 changed=1; in-band unchanged; CLAMPN 5 10 1 stays 5; below lo clamps up. Reconfirmed priority 50→9.
weaknesses.repro: CLAMPN 50 1 9 → 9 CHANGED 1

weaknesses.title: HASRESTPOS min wants careful use with SUBCMD (files only, not verb)
weaknesses.detail: Positive: HASRESTPOS 1 after SUBCMD set with routes; 0 when only verb. Prefer --name=val flags so bare flags do not eat targets.
weaknesses.repro: set -- --qps=10 r1 → HASRESTPOS 1

weaknesses.title: Dense LET tables break EACH AS and mid-EACH LET (unknown form)
weaknesses.detail: With ~10+ extra program LETs beyond a lean board, EACH LINE AS tid IN targets fails at SYS BLANK tid (unknown form tid). Nested EACH + LET hits = LAST fails earlier (unknown form hits). Predeclaring temps at top helps reassignment but steals more slots and can push past the threshold. Workarounds: slim unique LET/DEFAULT count; GREPV LAST chain; predeclare only essential temps (row/pref); avoid nested EACH in large boards. Isolated mini programs with few vars still nest EACH fine.
weaknesses.repro: mini2 + 10 LETs: EACH IN hits → unknown form hits; full board without slim: SYS BLANK tid unknown form tid

weaknesses.title: HELPFLAG/VERSIONFLAG halt before STATE write — no audit plate on banner path
weaknesses.detail: Correct CLI UX (EXIT 0 early) but ops agents cannot rely on CBI_REPORT for --help/--version invocations. banner subcmd is plate-visible miss-path snapshot of USAGE+PROG_VERSION+HIT knobs.
weaknesses.repro: run -- --help → halted stmts~28 no TICKETS/REPORT write

weaknesses.title: HELPFLAG+VERSIONFLAG miss path is quiet-friendly and sticky USAGE survives
weaknesses.detail: Positive: miss leaves HELPFLAG_HIT=0 VERSIONFLAG_HIT=0; program continues; USAGE sticky still available for REQUIRE tips and banner action.
weaknesses.repro: list after HELPFLAG miss → help_hit 0 ver_hit 0

weaknesses.title: SYS STR WORKERS hits host worker-count (nproc), not LET var WORKERS
weaknesses.detail: LET WORKERS=3; PRINT_JSON WORKERS shows 3, but SYS STR WORKERS yields nproc (here 4) and LAST_N=4. SYS STR workers (lowercase) binds the var. SYS NUM WORKERS is unknown form. Agents must not name ops vars WORKERS when feeding SYS STR/ITOA — use wcount/nworkers.
weaknesses.repro: LET WORKERS=3; SYS STR WORKERS → 4 on 4-cpu host; SYS STR wcount works

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGALL multi --tag bag + JOINLINES | for row fields
weaknesses.detail: Positive: --tag=canary --tag=eu → tag_n=2 bag; SYS JOINLINES "|" tags → canary|eu. OR default untagged when miss HIT=0. Coexists with GETFLAGN workers.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGALL tag OR untagged with two --tag → JOINLINES |

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGN/MS/BOOLFLAG OR ENV CLI>env>default with *_SRC
weaknesses.detail: Positive: export WORKERS=12 → GETFLAGN_SRC env; --workers=3 → cli; unset → default. FLAG_ENV set on env path. Probe-path GETFLAGMS timeout OR ENV TIMEOUT and BOOLFLAG force OR ENV FORCE confirmed.
weaknesses.repro: WORKERS=12 src env; --workers=3 src cli

weaknesses.title: Short -t alias collision risk across GETFLAGALL tag|t and GETFLAGMS timeout|t
weaknesses.detail: Prefer no short on tag when timeout also peels -t, or use distinct shorts. Board uses tag without short; timeout long-only in probe.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGALL tag|t with GETFLAGMS timeout|t same -t

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGCSV multi+comma+ENV chain with zone|zones|z aliases
weaknesses.detail: Positive: --zones=canary,eu --zone=apac → zone_n=3 JOINLINES canary|eu|apac; ENV ZONES=eu, us → 2 after space trim; CLI beats env; OR default 'default'. Coexists with GETFLAGN replicas.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGCSV zone|zones|z OR ENV ZONES OR default with multi flags

weaknesses.title: FLOORN/CAPN one-sided bounds after GETFLAGN (not CLAMPN)
weaknesses.detail: Positive: FLOORN 0 1 → 1; CAPN 100 16 → 16; mid 8 unchanged. Pipeline GETFLAGN then FLOORN then CAPN for replica floor/cap without dual-sided clamp. ATLEASTN/ATMOSTN aliases work in proof.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGN replicas 100; FLOORN 1; CAPN 16 → rcount 16

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGCSV needs zone|zones aliases for both --zone and --zones
weaknesses.detail: GETFLAGCSV zones|z alone does not peel --zone=apac (different stem). Agents must list zone|zones|z for long+short multi forms. Same class as flag alias explicitness.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGCSV zones|z with --zone=x may miss; zone|zones|z hits

weaknesses.title: DIVCEILN stole HOWMANY from COUNTWHERE (core before flow)
weaknesses.detail: DIVCEILN registered HOWMANY as alias in lang_ops_core; COUNTWHERE HOWMANY lives in lang_ops_flow (later). HOWMANY Counter tag 1 failed as DIVCEILN a b. Fixed: remove HOWMANY from DIVCEILN; keep PAGESN/CHUNKCOUNT/NPAGES. Same class as INRANGE/HASBETWEEN (W39).
weaknesses.repro: HOWMANY Counter tag 1 → DIVCEILN tip (pre-fix); COUNTWHERE works

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGPATH peels abs path + EXIST; CLI>ENV>default
weaknesses.detail: Positive: default include/cubalc_law.h EXIST=1 abs; ENV ARTIFACT=Makefile; --file=docs/... cli. Missing path still abs EXIST=0. Soft twin of REQUIRE FLAGFILE.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGPATH file OR ENV ARTIFACT OR include/cubalc_law.h

weaknesses.title: DIVCEILN/PAGESN page counts; div0 soft OK=0
weaknesses.detail: Positive: 100/16=7; 0/16=0; 10/0 → 0 sticky LAST_ERR. Pipeline SYS SIZE + DIVCEILN psize for artifact pages.
weaknesses.repro: DIVCEILN 100 16 → 7; DIVCEILN 10 0 → 0 DIVCEILN_OK 0

weaknesses.title: REQUIRE FLAGFILE miss sticky + usage tip; shell rc may be non-zero or 0
weaknesses.detail: Missing path with CUBALC_CPP_REQUIRE=1 sets ok:false + REQUIRE FLAGFILE err with usage tip. Observed shell $?=1 here (stronger than RESTPOS class). Soft GETFLAGPATH EXIST=0 preferred when agents need always-continue.
weaknesses.repro: CUBALC_CPP_REQUIRE=1 plan --file=no/such → REQUIRE FLAGFILE missing

weaknesses.title: RESTPATHS counts SUBCMD verb as a positional path
weaknesses.detail: After SUBCMD stage file1 file2, RESTPATHS_N=3: abspath(stage)+abs(file1)+abs(file2). RESTPATHS_EXIST_N counts only existing. Agents must DROPNTH 0 when basename matches ACTION after SUBCMD_HIT. RESTPATHS_EXIST_N is not recomputed after peel.
weaknesses.repro: SUBCMD stage; RESTPATHS with two files → n=3; DROPNTH 0 if basename=stage

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGDIR peels --out + mkdir -p; CREATED 0|1
weaknesses.detail: Positive: CLI --out=/tmp/x creates dir CREATED=1; second call CREATED=0; ENV OUTDIR chain; short -o. Empty miss OK=0 sticky LAST_ERR. Coexists with RESTPATHS files.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGDIR out|o OR ENV OUTDIR OR default → abs ISDIR

weaknesses.title: RESTPATHS missing inputs still absolute; EXIST_N soft
weaknesses.detail: Positive: no/such/x.bin + Makefile → path_n=2 exist_n=1 after subcmd peel; abs paths always. Good for inventory plates without hard fail.
weaknesses.repro: stage --out=D no/such Makefile → exist_n 1

weaknesses.title: NTHPOSPATH 0 is SUBCMD verb abs path (same class as RESTPATHS W61)
weaknesses.detail: export -- Makefile → NTHPOSPATH 0 = .../export EXIST=0; first file is NTHPOSPATH 1. Agents must use index 1 when SUBCMD_HIT, or peel verb. Probe confirmed nth0 ends with action name.
weaknesses.repro: SUBCMD export file; NTHPOSPATH 0 → verb; NTHPOSPATH 1 → file

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGOUT peels --report to abs file + mkdir parent for WRITE
weaknesses.detail: Positive: CLI/ENV/default create parent CREATED=1; LAST is file path not dir; WRITE digest works; second call CREATED=0 EXIST=1 when file present. Twin of GETFLAGDIR (dir) vs GETFLAGOUT (file).
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGOUT report OR ENV REPORT OR nested/out.json → WRITE LAST

weaknesses.title: ENSUREPARENT re-ensure after GETFLAGOUT is idempotent CREATED=0
weaknesses.detail: Positive: GETFLAGOUT already mkdirs parent; ENSUREPARENT out_file OK CREATED often 0. Useful dual for GETFLAGPATH+WRITE paths without FLAGOUT.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGOUT then ENSUREPARENT LAST

weaknesses.title: RESTPOSPATHS excludes SUBCMD verb (fixes RESTPATHS W61 class)
weaknesses.detail: Positive: seal Makefile h → RESTPOSPATHS_N=2 not 3. Probe: RESTPATHS_N=2 (probe+file) vs RESTPOSPATHS_N=1 (file only). Prefer RESTPOSPATHS after SUBCMD for file intake.
weaknesses.repro: SUBCMD seal a b; RESTPOSPATHS → n=2; RESTPATHS → n=3

weaknesses.title: WRITEOUT one-shot ENSUREPARENT+WRITE nested plates
weaknesses.detail: Positive: WRITEOUT nested/manifest body creates parents CREATED=1; second CREATED=0; LAST=abs file; LAST_N=bytes. PUTOUT/SYS WRITEOUT aliases. Coexists with GETFLAGOUT peel.
weaknesses.repro: WRITEOUT deep/m.txt body → ISFILE; parent mkdirs

weaknesses.title: SYS CAT with embedded newline in .cubalc source mangles body assembly
weaknesses.detail: Building multi-line manifest via SYS CAT body "\n" split across source lines duplicated schema and dropped basenames. Workaround: SYS PUSH body row for newline bags. Same class as REPLACEALL multiline hazard.
weaknesses.repro: SYS CAT body newline fragment in file → corrupt bag; SYS PUSH body row ok

weaknesses.title: APPENDOUT_CREATED is parent mkdir, not first-line; GETFLAGOUT steals create
weaknesses.detail: GETFLAGOUT log already mkdirs parent → APPENDOUT_CREATED often 0 even on first append. APPENDOUT_CREATED=1 only when parent was missing. Agents must not use CREATED as first-write detector; use ISFILE/LINES before append.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGOUT log; APPENDOUT log line → CREATED 0; APPENDOUT alone on fresh nest → CREATED 1

weaknesses.title: WRITEOUTATOMIC nested status plates; no leftover temps
weaknesses.detail: Positive: overwrite replaces body (ready→live); PATHGLOB *.cubalc-tmp empty; CREATED 0 on second write when parent exists.
weaknesses.repro: WRITEOUTATOMIC status ready; WRITEOUTATOMIC status live → only live

weaknesses.title: COPYOUT snaps status to nested dest; missing src soft OK=0
weaknesses.detail: Positive: COPYOUT status snap creates dest parents; soft fail on missing source. Snap action must pass same --status path as status write (fresh process peels defaults independently).
weaknesses.repro: COPYOUT stat_file snap_file; COPYOUT missing dest → OK 0

weaknesses.title: Eager multi GETFLAGOUT always mkdirs all default parents
weaknesses.detail: Board peels log+status+snap every invocation → creates default run/ trees under STATE even for list/log-only. Lazy peel per action would avoid side-effect dirs; costs more branches.
weaknesses.repro: list alone creates state/run/agent.log parent via default GETFLAGOUT

weaknesses.title: TOUCHOUT NEW vs CREATED: file create vs parent mkdir
weaknesses.detail: Positive: first TOUCHOUT NEW=1; renew NEW=0. CREATED often 0 after GETFLAGOUT already mkdirs parent (same class as APPENDOUT_CREATED W70). Prefer TOUCHOUT_NEW for lease claim vs renew.
weaknesses.repro: TOUCHOUT lease → NEW 1; TOUCHOUT again → NEW 0 CREATED 0

weaknesses.title: MOVEOUT promotes src to nested dest; src gone; missing soft
weaknesses.detail: Positive: MOVEOUT stage→live removes src; CREATED for dest parent; probe MOVEOUT missing → OK 0. Pass --src and --dest on promote invocation (fresh peels).
weaknesses.repro: MOVEOUT src dest; EXIST src 0; EXIST dest 1

weaknesses.title: WRITEOUT body with unquoted {braces} can parse as forms
weaknesses.detail: WRITEOUT path {"job":1} failed unknown form job in -e smoke. Prefer simple key=val plate lines or careful quoting. Board uses job=id claimed=ISO.
weaknesses.repro: WRITEOUT f {\"job\":1} → unknown form job

weaknesses.title: WRITEOUTIF mtime-stable when body unchanged
weaknesses.detail: Positive: first set CHANGED=1; same body CHANGED=0 and mtime unchanged after 1s sleep; different body CHANGED=1. Good for deploy status watchers. CREATED often 0 after GETFLAGOUT parent (W70 class).
weaknesses.repro: WRITEOUTIF st state=ready twice → second CHANGED 0 mtime stable

weaknesses.title: LOGSTAMP appends ISO Z + msg without DATE+CAT+APPENDOUT
weaknesses.detail: Positive: multi lines with ISO timestamps; LOGSTAMP_LINE/ISO knobs in proof; CREATED parent-only like APPENDOUT.
weaknesses.repro: LOGSTAMP log deploy-start → 2026-…Z deploy-start

weaknesses.title: LINKOUT creates abs symlink; re-link soft exists fail
weaknesses.detail: Positive: LINKOUT status latest → ISLINK abs target; second LINKOUT OK=0 sticky exists. Agents must RM link or tolerate soft miss for republish.
weaknesses.repro: LINKOUT st link; LINKOUT again → exists err

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGOUT realpath-follows existing symlinks to TARGET
weaknesses.detail: GETFLAGOUT link OR path when path is already a symlink returns realpath(target) with exist=1, not the link path. Agents that then RELINKOUT/RM that path destroy the plate file and recreate a symlink on the plate path. RELINKOUT itself carefully avoids realpath(linkpath); GETFLAGOUT undoes that safety. Workaround: GETFLAG (literal) for symlink destinations; GETFLAGOUT only for regular files/dirs that need parent mkdir.
weaknesses.repro: ln -s /tmp/t /tmp/l; GETFLAGOUT link OR /tmp/l -- --link=/tmp/l → LAST=/tmp/t not /tmp/l

weaknesses.title: VM vars[128] hard ceiling; new knobs silently fail when full
weaknesses.detail: Var table is fixed 128 slots (name[48]). Fat agent boards (IDENTITY+GETFLAGOUT×3+many LET/DEFAULT+CASE) reach n_vars≈127; subsequent var_set_num for RELINKOUT_CREATED/REPLACED and other op knobs silently no-ops (create returns NULL). Trace still prints C locals correctly while language knobs stay 0. Agents must lean LETs, reuse temps, or UNSET/DROP_VAR. VARS reports n; no hard-fail on overflow.
weaknesses.repro: board with ~50 LET + 3 GETFLAGOUT → VARS_N 127; RELINKOUT log replaced=1 but RELINKOUT_REPLACED still 0

weaknesses.title: HARDLINKOUT CREATED is parent-mkdir flag; re-dest soft exists
weaknesses.detail: Positive: HARDLINKOUT same-inode; CREATED often 0 after GETFLAGOUT already mkdirs parent (W70 class). Second HARDLINKOUT to same dest soft OK=0 exists. Prefer SAMEINODE for share verify.
weaknesses.repro: HARDLINKOUT src share; SAMEINODE 1; HARDLINKOUT again OK 0

weaknesses.title: RELINKOUT force-replaces nested symlink; fills LINKOUT re-link gap
weaknesses.detail: Positive: first link CREATED=1 REPLACED=0; retarget same path REPLACED=1 CREATED=0; READLINK peels new target. Closes W79/LINKOUT-force language_gap when agents use RELINKOUT and GETFLAG (not GETFLAGOUT) for the link path.
weaknesses.repro: RELINKOUT a cur; RELINKOUT b cur → REPLACED 1 READLINK b

weaknesses.title: CLAIMOUT exclusive nested claim; second soft exists; CREATED parent-only
weaknesses.detail: Positive: CLAIMOUT path body → HIT=1 CLAIM_PID>0 body on disk; second OK=0 HIT=0 soft held. CREATED often 0 after GETFLAGOUT parent mkdir (W70 class). Release via RM enables re-claim with CREATED=0 when parent exists. Body omit trailing NL (W5).
weaknesses.repro: CLAIMOUT f worker; CLAIMOUT f other → OK 0 HIT 0; RM f; CLAIMOUT f → HIT 1

weaknesses.title: TEEOUT writes nested plate and leaves body in LAST (not path)
weaknesses.detail: Positive: TEEOUT out body → LAST=body for HAS/GREP without READ; TEEOUT_PATH abs. CREATED parent-only like APPENDOUT. Distinct from WRITEOUT which leaves path-ish LAST. Agents that need path after write use TEEOUT_PATH not LAST.
weaknesses.repro: TEEOUT f rcpt=done; SYS HAS LAST rcpt= → 1; LAST is body not path

weaknesses.title: Custom CUBALC_* ENV reach SYS ENV; CUBALC_ARG* host still dead (W1/W9)
weaknesses.detail: Positive contrast: export CUBALC_CTQ_REQUIRE=1 is visible to SYS ENV and drives EXIT 2 on held claim. export CUBALC_ARG0=claim still does not populate SYS ARG (W1). Agents may use custom env gates but not ARG env contract.
weaknesses.repro: CUBALC_CTQ_REQUIRE=1 claim held → shell 2; CUBALC_ARG0=claim alone → list

weaknesses.title: RMTREE missing path is OK=1 with N=0 (idempotent, not soft-fail)
weaknesses.detail: Unlike CPTREE missing (OK=0 sticky missing) or empty path (OK=0 empty), RMTREE on a non-existent path returns OK=1 RMTREE_N=0. Agents cannot use OK alone to detect wipe-of-nothing vs wipe-of-tree; must check RMTREE_N or pre EXIST. Empty path still OK=0. Positive for GC scripts that re-run.
weaknesses.repro: RMTREE /no/such → OK 1 N 0; RMTREE "" → OK 0 empty

weaknesses.title: CPTREE recursive snapshot; refuses dest inside src; missing soft
weaknesses.detail: Positive: CPTREE work snap → N/BYTES knobs; nested files+empty dirs; source intact. CPTREE missing src OK=0; dest inside src OK=0 LAST_ERR contains inside. File-only CPTREE works. Agents use CPTREE_N/CPTREE_BYTES not LAST alone (LAST is abs dest path).
weaknesses.repro: CPTREE src dst N>=5; CPTREE src src/inside → dest inside src

weaknesses.title: RMTREE removes file or full dir tree; N counts nodes
weaknesses.detail: Positive: RMTREE work after stage+snap removed 6 nodes; EXIST work 0; sibling snap untouched until separate wipe. RMNEST/RMRF aliases. Pair with CPTREE for stage→snap→wipe sandbox lifecycle.
weaknesses.repro: RMTREE work → N 6 EXIST 0; snap still present

weaknesses.title: DIRSIZE recursive file-byte inventory; FILES/DIRS knobs
weaknesses.detail: Positive: DIRSIZE stage → DIRSIZE/LAST_N=bytes, DIRSIZE_FILES, DIRSIZE_DIRS (empty dirs counted). Missing path OK=0 soft. LAST string is abs path after op; agents must read DIRSIZE or LAST_N for bytes not LAST string. Good for deploy size gates with MAXB.
weaknesses.repro: DIRSIZE tree → bytes 15 files 2 dirs 3; DIRSIZE missing → OK 0

weaknesses.title: MVTREE_N is 1 on same-FS rename, not recursive node count
weaknesses.detail: Same-filesystem MVTREE uses rename(2): MVTREE_RENAMED=1 and MVTREE_N=1 even for multi-file trees. Cross-device path may CPTREE+RMTREE with higher N. Agents must not treat MVTREE_N as CPTREE_N-style node inventory; use DIRSIZE/EXIST for post-promote checks. Dest-inside-src and missing soft like CPTREE.
weaknesses.repro: MVTREE stage live with 5 nodes → RENAMED 1 N 1; EXIST stage 0

weaknesses.title: EQTREE OK=1 on both equal and unequal; equality is EQTREE/LAST_N
weaknesses.detail: EQTREE always OK=1 when both paths exist; equal → EQTREE=1 LAST_N=1; differ → EQTREE=0 LAST_N=0 with EQTREE_REASON content|missing|extra_b and EQTREE_DIFF path fragment. Soft OK=0 only for missing/empty args. Agents that branch on OK alone will false-admit drift. Board uses eq_n + EXIT under REQUIRE.
weaknesses.repro: EQTREE a b equal OK1 EQTREE1; mutate b → OK1 EQTREE0 reason content

weaknesses.title: GREPTREE is literal substring, not whole-word token match
weaknesses.detail: GREPTREE root needle scans file contents as substring (like grep without word boundaries). Needle SECRE matches SECRET_ABC; plain 'no secret here' hits GREPTREEI secret. Agents needing exact tokens must post-filter LAST path bag or use longer unique needles. GREPTREE_N=0 is still OK=1 (empty hit set is success).
weaknesses.repro: seed SECRET_ABC; GREPTREE SECRE → N>=1; GREPTREE zzz → OK1 N0

weaknesses.title: GREPTREE returns path bag + SCAN count; GREPTREEI for case-fold
weaknesses.detail: Positive: LAST is multiline paths of matching files; GREPTREE_N file hits; GREPTREE_SCAN files examined. GREPTREEI finds WARNING via warning. Missing root OK=0; empty path OK=0. Distinct from bag SYS GREP which is line-level in memory.
weaknesses.repro: GREPTREE base error → err.log; GREPTREEI base warning → warn.log

weaknesses.title: REPLACETREE bulk REPLACEALL; N=files SUBS=replacements; empty old no-op
weaknesses.detail: Positive: REPLACETREE root old new rewrites nested files; REPLACETREE_N files touched; REPLACETREE_SUBS total substitutions. Second pass when already replaced → N=0 SUBS=0 OK=1. Empty old string no-op OK=1. Missing root soft OK=0. LAST is path bag of rewritten files.
weaknesses.repro: REPLACETREE base OLD NEW → N2 SUBS3; again → N0

weaknesses.title: COUNTINTREE tallies substring occurrences + FILES; zero is OK=1
weaknesses.detail: Positive: COUNTINTREE root needle → COUNTINTREE/LAST_N total hits, COUNTINTREE_FILES files with ≥1 hit. Empty needle → 0. Missing root soft OK=0. COUNTINTREEI case-fold. Unlike GREPTREE (path bag), this returns a number for SLO/severity budgets (MAXC gate). Substring class same as GREPTREE (W93): erro counts inside error.
weaknesses.repro: COUNTINTREE logs error → 2; COUNTINTREE zzz → OK1 N0; missing → OK0

weaknesses.title: GREPLINESTREE harvests matching lines (not paths); FILES separate
weaknesses.detail: Positive: GREPLINESTREE root needle → LAST multiline line bag, GREPLINESTREE_N line count, GREPLINESTREE_FILES file count. Distinct from GREPTREE path list and COUNTINTREE occurrence tally. Zero match OK=1 N=0. GREPLINESTREEI/HARVESTTREE aliases. Harvest bag last line may omit final NL (W5/W10 class) when written to plate.
weaknesses.repro: GREPLINESTREE logs error → 2 lines boom/again; GREPTREE would return err.log path only

weaknesses.title: Tree search family OK=1 on empty hits; soft only on missing root
weaknesses.detail: GREPTREE/COUNTINTREE/GREPLINESTREE all succeed with N=0 when needle absent. Agents cannot use OK for 'found something' — must branch on N/COUNT/LAST_N. REQUIRE-style hard fail needs board EXIT after N check or missing-root soft. Reconfirms W93 empty-hit pattern across tree ops.
weaknesses.repro: COUNTINTREE/GREPLINESTREE zzz → OK1 N0; harvest board marks miss only via line_n>0 gate

weaknesses.title: FIRSTINTREE/LASTINTREE one-shot path pick; HIT=0 empty OK=1
weaknesses.detail: Positive: FIRSTINTREE root needle → LAST abs path, FIRSTINTREE_HIT 0|1. LASTINTREE last DFS match. No-match OK=1 HIT=0 LAST empty (same W98 empty-hit class). Order is sorted DFS (a/b/mid before a/err). FIRSTINTREEI/LASTINTREEI case-fold. Distinct from GREPTREE multi-path bag.
weaknesses.repro: FIRSTINTREE logs error → …/mid.txt; LASTINTREE → …/err.log; zzz → HIT 0 OK 1

weaknesses.title: FIRSTLINEINTREE peels line text + PATH + 0-based I
weaknesses.detail: Positive: FIRSTLINEINTREE → LAST=line body, FIRSTLINEINTREE_PATH file, FIRSTLINEINTREE_I line index (0-based; miss I=-1). LASTLINEINTREE last match across tree. No-match OK=1 HIT=0 PATH empty. Agents get path+line without GREPLINESTREE+TAKE. Substring needle (erro) still hits.
weaknesses.repro: FIRSTLINEINTREE error → 'error first-line' I=1 path mid.txt; miss → HIT0 I=-1

weaknesses.title: Tree first/last order is sorted DFS path order, not mtime/inode
weaknesses.detail: FIRST/LASTINTREE and FIRST/LASTLINEINTREE walk sorted DFS (lexical path), not filesystem discovery or chronological mtime. 'Last error' means last path/line in that order, not newest wall-clock event. Incident agents needing recency must use mtime-aware forms or sort plates separately.
weaknesses.repro: a/b/mid before a/err.log even if err.log written later on disk

weaknesses.title: PATHLINETREE is substring grep -rn; colon needle matches any ':' line
weaknesses.detail: PATHLINETREE root needle returns path:lineno:text bags (1-based lineno). Needle ':' hits every line containing a colon (error: boom, WARNING: careful) — useful multi-file count but a false friend if agents mean field separators. Empty hits OK=1 N=0 (W98 class). Text after second colon may itself contain colons (error: boom).
weaknesses.repro: PATHLINETREE logs error → N2; PATHLINETREE logs : → N3 FILES2

weaknesses.title: PARSEPATHLINE peels first two colon fields as path and lineno
weaknesses.detail: Positive: PARSEPATHLINE path:N:text → PATH, LINE_N, LAST/TEXT=remainder (colons kept in body). Plain lines HIT=0 OK=1. Empty string soft OK=0. Agents building digests from PATHLINETREE bags must NTH then PARSEPATHLINE; HIT distinguishes annotated vs garbage fields.
weaknesses.repro: PARSEPATHLINE /p:10:a:b:c → PATH /p LINE_N 10 LAST a:b:c; plain → HIT 0

weaknesses.title: PATHLINEPATHS unique first-seen paths; SKIP non-annotated
weaknesses.detail: Positive: PATHLINEPATHS bag → unique paths in first-seen order, PATHLINEPATHS_N, SKIP count for lines that fail path:num:text shape. Empty bag OK=1 N=0. Companion to PATHLINETREE for implicated-file lists without EACH+HASLINE glue.
weaknesses.repro: PATHLINEPATHS three cites two files → N2; plain line increments SKIP

weaknesses.title: PATHLINETEXTS peels message bodies; keeps duplicates; SKIP plain
weaknesses.detail: Positive: PATHLINETEXTS bag → text-only bag in bag order, PATHLINETEXTS_N, SKIP non-annotated. Duplicates preserved (FREQ-ready). Empty bag OK=1 N=0. Empty body path:N: still counts as one field. Companion to PATHLINEPATHS (unique files) without EACH+PARSEPATHLINE.
weaknesses.repro: PATHLINETREE error; PATHLINETEXTS LAST → 3x 'error: boom' + other

weaknesses.title: PATHLINEFREQ path:count bag is first-seen order, not sorted by count
weaknesses.detail: PATHLINEFREQ returns unique path:count lines in first-seen pathline order (DFS harvest order), not descending frequency. TOPKEY/LOOKUPN give hottest path and counts. Agents that NTH 0 expecting max heat will get first-seen file (often warn before err). TOTAL counts annotated lines; SKIP plain. Empty bag OK=1 TOTAL 0.
weaknesses.repro: err 3 hits warn 1; VAL may list warn:1 before err:3; TOPKEY ends err.log

weaknesses.title: PATHLINEFREQ TOTAL vs N: lines vs unique paths
weaknesses.detail: Positive: PATHLINEFREQ_N = unique paths, PATHLINEFREQ_TOTAL = cite lines, SKIP = garbage fields. LOOKUPN path → count. Good for MAXT budgets on total hits and TOPKEY for hottest file. Distinct from COUNTINTREE (global substring tally without path hist).
weaknesses.repro: 4 error cites / 2 files → N2 TOTAL4; LOOKUPN err.log → 3

weaknesses.title: PARSEPATHLINE round-trip after FORMATPATHLINE can HIT=0 under agent boards
weaknesses.detail: FORMATPATHLINE builds valid path:lineno:text and VAL stores it, but PARSEPATHLINE on a LET-bound copy immediately after can yield PARSEPATHLINE_HIT=0 in deep INCLUDE agent_boot boards (reproduced once on cite arm; lean -e sequence HIT=1). Agents should trust FORMAT OK+LAST for cite emit; use PARSE on literals or fresh peels for intake. Possible LAST/knob clobber or var-table pressure near W81.
weaknesses.repro: board cite arm: FORMATPATHLINE ok cite string; PARSEPATHLINE out → HIT 0 intermittently/in-board

weaknesses.title: TAKEINTREE first n matching paths DFS; n=0 empty OK=1
weaknesses.detail: Positive: TAKEINTREE root needle n → path bag TAKEINTREE_N≤n, MAX=n. Oversize n caps at match count. n=0 → N=0 empty LAST OK=1. Missing root soft OK=0. Order matches FIRSTINTREE head. TAKEINTREEI case-fold. Good for triage samples without full GREPTREE bag.
weaknesses.repro: TAKEINTREE logs error 2 → mid+z; TAKE 0 → N0; TAKE 10 → N3

weaknesses.title: NTHINTREE 0-based; OOR and negative soft HIT=0 OK=1
weaknesses.detail: Positive: NTHINTREE root needle i → path, NTHINTREE_HIT, NTHINTREE_I. i=0 equals FIRSTINTREE. Out-of-range or negative → HIT=0 empty LAST OK=1 (not soft path miss). Distinct from SYS NTH on bags (no tree walk). INDEXINTREE alias.
weaknesses.repro: NTHINTREE error 1 → z.txt; NTH 9 → HIT 0; NTH -1 → HIT 0

weaknesses.title: FORMATPATHLINE builds path:lineno:text; inverse of PARSEPATHLINE
weaknesses.detail: Positive: FORMATPATHLINE path lineno text → LAST cite; sticky PATH/LINE_N/TEXT. Empty path soft OK=0. Omitted text can use LAST. Round-trip with FIRSTLINEINTREE: use I+1 for 1-based grep -n lines (I is 0-based). Text may contain colons.
weaknesses.repro: FORMATPATHLINE /p 2 'a:b' → /p:2:a:b; FIRSTLINE I=1 → lineno 2

weaknesses.title: HASINTREE keeps LAST string; path only in PATH/HASINTREE_PATH (not LAST)
weaknesses.detail: HASLINE-style: after HASINTREE hit, LAST stays prior string (board VAL wrote preserve-me). Path is PATH and HASINTREE_PATH. Agents that LET out=LAST after probe get the preserved token not the match path. Good for IF guards; false friend for VAL/out capture. SLICEINTREE correctly puts path bag in LAST.
weaknesses.repro: SYS JOIN '' keep; HASINTREE root error; LAST==keep; PATH ends mid.txt

weaknesses.title: SLICEINTREE start/count are 0-based window; past-end and count0 both soft empty OK=1 N=0
weaknesses.detail: No hard OOR: start past hits and count 0 return empty bag with OK=1. Agents must treat N==0 as empty page (soft FAIL or REQUIRE EXIT). Matches TAKEINTREE empty style. Mid page start1 count1 equals NTHINTREE 1 path.
weaknesses.repro: SLICEINTREE root error 9 2 → N=0 OK=1; count 0 → N=0

weaknesses.title: HASINTREE/SLICEINTREE walk order is sorted DFS (same family as TAKE/FIRST)
weaknesses.detail: Hits order mid.txt then z.txt then err.log under nested a/b. No mtime/reverse window. Agents cannot page 'newest first' without sort glue.
weaknesses.repro: SLICE 0 2 error → mid then z not err.log first

weaknesses.title: JSON / JSONHAS / JSON key FROM reject variable key tokens (literals only)
weaknesses.detail: Same class as HASFLAG (W13): SYS JSONHAS k plate with k=version looks for field name k not value. Agents must EQS-branch known keys into literal peels. Breaks dynamic key loops from JSONKEYS bag without CASE glue.
weaknesses.repro: LET k version; JSONHAS k plate → HIT 0; JSONHAS "version" → 1

weaknesses.title: JSONKEYS lists object-valued keys but JSONHAS/JSON peel miss them
weaknesses.detail: Plate nested:{x:1} appears in JSONKEYS bag, but JSONHAS nested and JSON nested FROM both miss (HIT=0/OK=0). Only scalar fields peel. Nested object access needs a separate path or string re-parse. False friend for agent schema discovery→peel pipelines.
weaknesses.repro: JSONKEYS has nested; JSONHAS nested → 0; JSON nested FROM → miss

weaknesses.title: CLEAR_ERR intentionally sets LAST string to cleared
weaknesses.detail: var_set_str LAST=cleared after wipe. Conflicts with JSONHAS/HASINTREE LAST-preserve (W112): board that JOIN preserve then CLEAR_ERR after probe loses the token; VAL became cleared. Capture LAST into a LET before CLEAR_ERR.
weaknesses.repro: JOIN preserve-me; CLEAR_ERR; LAST is cleared not preserve-me

weaknesses.title: JSONOBJ/JSONSET reject bare numeric vars as values
weaknesses.detail: LET TN=3; SYS JSONOBJ "n" TN → missing value hard err. SYS JSONSET plate "n" TN → unknown form TN. String vars and literals work. Agents must SYS STR TN; LET n_str=LAST before pair writes. Side effect: n stored as JSON string "3" not number.
weaknesses.repro: LET TN 3; JSONOBJ "n" TN fails; STR then JSONOBJ "n" n_str ok

weaknesses.title: STR shuttle for W118 demotes numbers to JSON strings
weaknesses.detail: After SYS STR TN + JSONSET n n_str, plate has "n":"3" not "n":3. Peers that type-check JSON numbers may fail. No JSONSETN / typed numeric put. Literals 3 in JSONOBJ keep number type.
weaknesses.repro: mint with n_str → cat plate shows "n":"0"

weaknesses.title: JSONOBJ FROM base reports only new pair count not total keys
weaknesses.detail: JSONOBJ FROM body "extra" "yes" "stamp_n" n_str → JSONOBJ_N=2 (added pairs) not full key count. Agents must JSONKEYS after extend for inventory. Positive for delta tracking.
weaknesses.repro: extend existing 6-key plate → JSONOBJ_N 2

weaknesses.title: DROPINTREE negative skip clamps to 0 silently (SKIP knob != arg)
weaknesses.detail: DROPINTREE root error -1 → N=3 SKIP=0 OK=1. No hard err. Board GETFLAGN --skip=-1 leaves SK=-1 while op used 0. Agents comparing SK plate to DROPINTREE_SKIP can disagree. Prefer clamp or hard reject negatives.
weaknesses.repro: DROPINTREE root error -1 → SKIP 0 N all; flag SK still -1

weaknesses.title: tree content needles are substrings not whole-token (err matches error)
weaknesses.detail: DROPINTREE root err 0 hits all three error* files (mid/z/err.log). Same class as GREP substring. Agents wanting whole-word need post-filter or exact line ops. False friend for short needles.
weaknesses.repro: DROPINTREE root err 0 → N=3 same as error

weaknesses.title: skip past end / skip==hitcount both soft empty OK=1 N=0
weaknesses.detail: DROP skip 3 or 99 on 3 hits → empty bag no hard OOR. Dual TAKE+DROP cover works (1+2=3). Residual empty is agent FAIL/REQUIRE EXIT concern not language hard fail.
weaknesses.repro: DROPINTREE root error 3 → N=0 OK=1

weaknesses.title: JSONINC delta and JSONENSURE value reject numeric vars (literal only)
weaknesses.detail: SYS JSONINC body "retries" DELTA → unknown form DELTA (partial default +1 then hard fail). SYS JSONENSURE body "max" MAXR same. STR shuttle works for ENSURE values (max stored as string "10", JSONN peels 10). INC delta cannot use string var either — only literal 1/2/3/5 EQS branches.
weaknesses.repro: LET d 2; JSONINC p retries d → unknown form d; JSONINC p retries 2 ok

weaknesses.title: JSONN OR fallback requires numeric literal not variable
weaknesses.detail: SYS JSONN "max" FROM body OR MAXR hard-fails usage form. OR 10 works. Same literal-only class as W115/W124. Agents cannot pass CLI --max into OR without branching.
weaknesses.repro: JSONN max FROM p OR MAXR fails; OR 10 ok

weaknesses.title: JSONN non-numeric string HIT=1 LAST_N=0 (role→0)
weaknesses.detail: Positive: peel role as agent string leaves LAST=role LAST_N=0 without soft fail. Distinguish from miss (OK=0). Useful but easy to treat as zero counter.
weaknesses.repro: JSONN role FROM plate → HIT1 LAST_N0 LAST=worker

weaknesses.title: JSONPICK emits keys in pick-list order not original plate order
weaknesses.detail: Pick ok,n,role,schema from plate ordered schema,ok,... yields {"ok":1,"n":5,"role":...,"schema":...}. Agents that rely on key order for signatures/diff may break. Prefer JSONKEYS after pick for inventory.
weaknesses.repro: JSONPICK plate ok n role schema → ok first not schema

weaknesses.title: JSONRENAME overwrites destination key silently
weaknesses.detail: RENAME a→b when b exists: new b gets a's value, old b dropped, N=1. No conflict soft flag. Schema migrate can clobber live fields without warning.
weaknesses.repro: JSONRENAME {a:10,b:20} a b → b=10 only

weaknesses.title: JSONPICK all-missing keys → {} OK=1 N=0 soft
weaknesses.detail: No hard fail when none of listed keys present. DROP all-miss leaves plate unchanged N=0. RENAME miss N=0 plate intact. Agents need N>0 gates for export contracts.
weaknesses.repro: JSONPICK {a:1} zzz → LAST {} N=0 OK=1

weaknesses.title: FLAG and KEY are host specials — user vars named FLAG/KEY mis-bind
weaknesses.detail: DEFAULT FLAG="debug"; GETFLAG flag → debug; GETFLAG key → n; then LET flag_name=FLAG binds wrong (toggled n not debug). PRINT FLAG is not the var. Same class as note (W29). Use FLAG_S/KEY_S or other names.
weaknesses.repro: LET FLAG debug; GETFLAG key; LET x=FLAG → not debug; JSONTOGGLE body FLAG hits wrong key

weaknesses.title: JSONTYPE/JSONTOGGLE accept string var keys; JSONN/JSON still literal-only
weaknesses.detail: SYS JSONTYPE body KEY_S and JSONTOGGLE body flag_name work. SYS JSONN KEY_S FROM body looks for field KEY_S (miss). Agents need EQS branches for peel after type gate. Inconsistent key resolution across JSON family.
weaknesses.repro: LET k n; JSONTYPE p k → num; JSONN k FROM p → no field KEY_S

weaknesses.title: JSONTOGGLE treats any non-zero/non-empty as truthy → 0 (can zero counters)
weaknesses.detail: Toggle on n=7 → n=0; tag="on" → 0. Missing→1 is intentional. Wrong flag name that collides with a counter (or W130 FLAG bug) silently zeros data. Prefer dedicated bool keys only.
weaknesses.repro: JSONTOGGLE {n:7} n → n=0 PREV truthy

weaknesses.title: CLEAR_ERR after SETMATCH/MOVELINE before LET bag=LAST stores cleared
weaknesses.detail: W117 CLEAR_ERR sets LAST=cleared. Board SETMATCH hit then CLEAR_ERR then LET rost_bag=LAST wrote ROSTER.txt as the word cleared. Must capture LAST into a var immediately after bag mutators, before CLEAR_ERR/CAT.
weaknesses.repro: SETMATCH bag a A; CLEAR_ERR; LET bag=LAST → bag is cleared

weaknesses.title: COUNTLINE/SETMATCH are exact full-field only (not substring)
weaknesses.detail: Positive for peer:status rows: COUNTLINE bag idle → 0 while GREP :idle → 3. SETMATCH ERROR boom bag with needle ERROR misses; needs full field. Agents mixing GREP substring tallies with COUNTLINE exact get false zeros.
weaknesses.repro: COUNTLINE peer1:idle\n... idle → 0; COUNTLINE peer1:idle → 1

weaknesses.title: MOVELINE from OOR soft N=0; dest past end clamps to last
weaknesses.detail: MOVELINE bag 5 0 on 3 lines → N=0 bag unchanged. MOVELINE 0 99 clamps to end (success). FINDLINE miss OK=0 LAST_N=-1 (not 0) — agents must not treat N==0 as only miss.
weaknesses.repro: FINDLINE miss LAST_N=-1; MOVELINE 0 99 clamps

weaknesses.title: JSONSWAP one-missing key becomes silent move (rename)
weaknesses.detail: SWAP a↔b when only a present: a removed, b=a value, N=1. Both missing N=0 soft. Agents expecting hard dual-present swap can lose keys. Documented as feature in proof; still a dual-buffer footgun.
weaknesses.repro: JSONSWAP {a:7} a b → {b:7} no a

weaknesses.title: SUM on JSONVALUES mixed plate silently sums only numerics
weaknesses.detail: VALUES bag includes schema/role/ts strings; SYS SUM LAST → 35 (=ok+cur+prev+n+snap) with no err. Agents using SUM for plate health can ignore non-numeric fields without warning. Prefer pick numeric keys first.
weaknesses.repro: JSONVALUES full status plate; SUM → 35 not fail

weaknesses.title: JSONCOPY overwrites destination key silently (same class as RENAME W128)
weaknesses.detail: COPY a→b when b exists replaces b with a raw value. No conflict flag. Snapshot into prev after bump can clobber intentional prev if order wrong — board copies cur→prev before INC to avoid.
weaknesses.repro: JSONCOPY {a:10,b:20} a b → b=10

weaknesses.title: JSONEMPTY LAST_N polarity is 1=empty 0=nonempty (easy IF invert)
weaknesses.detail: JSONEMPTY {} → LAST_N 1; nonempty plate → LAST_N 0. JSONNONEMPTY is inverse. Agents writing IF LAST_N for 'has data' on EMPTY get the wrong branch. Prefer JSONNONEMPTY or JSONLEN > 0 for presence gates.
weaknesses.repro: JSONEMPTY {a:1} → LAST_N 0; JSONEMPTY {} → 1

weaknesses.title: JSONLEN/EMPTY/SUMN treat non-object as empty/0 with OK=1
weaknesses.detail: Arrays and garbage strings: LEN=0 EMPTY=1 SUMN=0 all soft success. Bad peer plates look like empty objects. Agents need JSONTYPE or STARTS { before health gates.
weaknesses.repro: JSONEMPTY [1,2] → LAST_N 1 OK=1; JSONLEN not-json → 0

weaknesses.title: JSONSUMN includes bool as 0|1 and skips strings silently
weaknesses.detail: Positive vs W137 VALUES+SUM: SUMN is typed and documented. ok=true adds 1; dry=false adds 0; schema/role/ts ignored. Score gates can inflate by flag keys — PICK counters before SUMN for pure tallies.
weaknesses.repro: SUMN {ok:true,n:7,s:hi} → 8

weaknesses.title: JSONMAXN/MINN/TOPKEY/BOTKEY count bools as 0|1
weaknesses.detail: Same class as JSONSUMN (W141): true→1 false→0 enter extreme math. Load plate with live:true makes MINN=1 and BOTKEY=live instead of coldest shard. Pure-numeric PICK before extremes, or mint without bool flags.
weaknesses.repro: JSONOBJ s0 12 s1 3 live true s2 40; JSONMINN → 1; JSONBOTKEY → live

weaknesses.title: JSONTOPKEY/BOTKEY overwrite LAST with key; MAXN keeps plate
weaknesses.detail: Asymmetric LAST contract: JSONMAXN/MINN set LAST=plate + LAST_N=v (chain peel ok). JSONTOPKEY/BOTKEY set LAST=key + LAST_N=v so subsequent JSONN FROM LAST fails. Agents must LET key=LAST then peel FROM saved plate body. Easy footgun when mixing value+key extremes in one flow.
weaknesses.repro: JSONTOPKEY plate; JSONN k FROM LAST → miss; must JSONN k FROM body

weaknesses.title: Op side-channel vars (JSONAVGN_N/USED etc) silent-fail at n_vars=128
weaknesses.detail: VM var table hard-caps at 128 (lang_core var_find create). Host op still computes (trace avg=5 used=3) and sets LAST_N, but var_set_num for new names JSONAVGN_N/JSONAVGN_USED returns without binding when full. LET x = JSONAVGN_N → 0 and gates deny/admit wrongly. Heavy agent_boot+GETFLAG*+locals boards hit this. Prefer LET x = LAST_N immediately; use JSONLEN for field counts instead of JSONAVGN_USED.
weaknesses.repro: full contract board gate: trace avg=5 but LET avg_n=JSONAVGN_N → 0 until capture LAST_N

weaknesses.title: JSONAVGN counts bools 0|1 and truncates toward 0
weaknesses.detail: Same bool pollution class as SUMN/MAXN (W141/W142). (1+2)/2→1 trunc. PICK pure metrics before mean for SLO gates.
weaknesses.repro: JSONAVGN {ok:true,flag:false,n:9,s:hi} → 3 used 3; {x:1,y:2} → 1

weaknesses.title: JSONEQ is exact key-set equality; extra keys fail even if required fields match
weaknesses.detail: Peer with extra noise fails JSONEQ; use JSONSUBSET for required-field admit and JSONEQ only for full snapshot verify. SUPERSET dual of SUBSET. Documented positive: status⊆peer_with_extra SUBSET=1 EQ=0.
weaknesses.repro: EQ status vs status+extra → 0; SUBSET status peer → 1

weaknesses.title: JSONMISS/PRESENT overwrite LAST with key bag; HASALL keeps plate
weaknesses.detail: Asymmetric LAST contract (class of W143 TOPKEY): HASALL/HASANY keep plate for chain peel; MISS/PRESENT set LAST=newline bag of keys and LAST_N=count. Agents that JSONMISS then JSONN FROM LAST fail. Capture miss_bag=LAST then peel FROM body.
weaknesses.repro: JSONMISS plate keys; JSONN k FROM LAST → miss; use saved body

weaknesses.title: null and false count as present keys (not missing)
weaknesses.detail: JSONHASALL/MISS treat key existence only — gone:null and flag:false are present. Ops handoffs that mean 'unset' via null still pass presence gates. Pair with JSONTYPE or value SUBSET for semantic completeness.
weaknesses.repro: JSONHASALL {gone:null,flag:false,n:0} gone flag n → 1; MISS other only

weaknesses.title: Empty key list: HASALL→1 HASANY→0
weaknesses.detail: Vacuous all-of-empty is true; any-of-empty is false. Surprising in dynamic OF bag when need list is blank after GREPV.
weaknesses.repro: JSONHASALL plate → 1; JSONHASANY plate → 0

weaknesses.title: SYS NTH has no OF bag form — only indexes LAST
weaknesses.detail: Proof 1082 does NTH after PLUCK leaves bag in LAST. SYS NTH 0 OF val_bag is unknown form OF. Agents must re-PLUCK or keep bag in LAST before each NTH; cannot random-access a saved bag without rebinding LAST.
weaknesses.repro: SYS NTH 0 OF val_bag → unknown form OF; SYS JSONPLUCK …; SYS NTH 0 works

weaknesses.title: PRINT_JSON collapses multi-line bag newlines
weaknesses.detail:
EXTRA key bag noise
debug and PLUCK 10
2
 render as noisedebug / 102 in PRINT_JSON objects. STATUS rows via CAT+HASLINE still see real newlines. Agents logging bags via PRINT_JSON lose field boundaries.
weaknesses.repro: PRINT_JSON key_bag after JSONEXTRA → "noisedebug"

weaknesses.title: REQUIRE JSONHASALL fail → shell 1, plate exit_code 0
weaknesses.detail: Missing keys set asserts_fail+err message listing missing, shell often 1, but exit_code stays 0 (W7 class). Soft twin SYS JSONHASALL + EXIT n under REQUIRE env is more reliable for ops shell contracts.
weaknesses.repro: REQUIRE JSONHASALL {a:1} a z → asserts_fail 1 exit_code 0 shell 1

weaknesses.title: JSONEXACT is key-set only — values may drift while EXACT=1
weaknesses.detail: Exact schema gates presence/absence of keys, not value types or contents. role can change worker→boss, ok 1→0, still EXACT. Pair with JSONSUBSET/EQ for value contracts after EXACT admit.
weaknesses.repro: JSONEXACT {schema,role,ok,load,zone} match; mutate ok=0 still EXACT=1

weaknesses.title: REQUIRE JSONONLY/JSONEXACT fail → shell 1 exit_code 0 (W152 class)
weaknesses.detail: Same assert-fail path as REQUIRE JSONHASALL: lists missing/extra in err, asserts_fail=1, shell often 1, plate exit_code 0. Soft JSONEXACT + EXIT n under env is more reliable for ops.
weaknesses.repro: REQUIRE JSONONLY {a,noise} a b → shell 1 exit_code 0

weaknesses.title: JSONONLY allow-list may be a superset — missing keys still pass ONLY
weaknesses.detail: REQUIRE JSONONLY {a:1} a b c succeeds (no extras). ONLY ≠ EXACT. Agents needing both must JSONEXACT or HASALL+ONLY dual.
weaknesses.repro: REQUIRE JSONONLY {a:1} a b c → ok; JSONEXACT same → fail miss b c

weaknesses.title: JSONDELTA arg order is old,new (values from NEW) — silent swap hazard
weaknesses.detail: SYS JSONDELTA prev cur peels NEW values; swapped args silently produce OLD values for shared keys and wrong patch payloads. No order-check or keyword default beyond FROM NEW|OLD. Agents must document call site as old,new.
weaknesses.repro: JSONDELTA new old → load from old; JSONDELTA old new → load from new

weaknesses.title: KEYDIFF is keys-only; value-only edits leave KEYDIFF empty
weaknesses.detail: Same key-set plates with m:2→9: KEYDIFF=0 CHANGED=1. Ops using KEYDIFF alone miss value drift. Pair KEYDIFF+CHANGED or use DELTA.
weaknesses.repro: KEYDIFF {k:1,m:2}{k:1,m:9}→0; CHANGED→m

weaknesses.title: DELTA keeps LAST as patch plate; KEYDIFF/CHANGED set LAST to key bag
weaknesses.detail: Asymmetric LAST (W143/W147 class): after DELTA peel JSONN works; after CHANGED LAST is bag not plate. Capture bags immediately; do not chain peels after KEYDIFF.
weaknesses.repro: JSONCHANGED a b; JSONN k FROM LAST → fail; JSONDELTA a b; JSONN k FROM LAST ok

weaknesses.title: REQUIRE JSONEQ/SUBSET fail → shell 1 exit_code 0 (W152 class)
weaknesses.detail: Mismatch lists changed/bad keys in err (positive UX) but asserts_fail path leaves plate exit_code 0 and shell often 1. Soft JSONEQ/SUBSET + EXIT n under env is reliable for ops shell contracts.
weaknesses.repro: REQUIRE JSONEQ {a:1}{a:2} → err lists a, shell 1 exit_code 0

weaknesses.title: Hard REQUIRE alone is assert-fail not EXIT — agents need soft-first + EXIT n
weaknesses.detail: Board pattern soft IF then REQUIRE only on match avoids assert-fail pollution; on soft deny use EXIT n under CUBALC_*_REQUIRE. Documented as agent contract: never bare REQUIRE for process rc.
weaknesses.repro: soft deny path EXIT 2 under REQUIRE env; bare REQUIRE JSONEQ mismatch exit_code 0

weaknesses.title: EQ deny with SUBSET still true is common lockstep split
weaknesses.detail: Value drift on non-required fields fails EQ while SUBSET/COVERS pass. Gate must compose both for full lockstep; SUBSET alone is not lockstep.
weaknesses.repro: load 10→99: EQ0 SUBSET1 CHANGED load

weaknesses.title: JSONDEFAULTS LAST_N is inserted-count not plate size
weaknesses.detail: LAST_N/JSONDEFAULTS_N = keys filled this call; complete re-apply yields 0. Agents checking boot success must not treat LAST_N==0 as failure when plate already complete — pair with HASALL or JSONDEFAULTS_HAD.
weaknesses.repro: DEFAULTS complete plate → LAST_N 0 HAD>0; empty {} defs → LAST_N full

weaknesses.title: REQUIRE JSONNEQ keeps LAST as first plate (prev) not cur
weaknesses.detail: After REQUIRE JSONNEQ prev body, peel FROM LAST reads prev. Chain peel of mutated load wrong unless peel FROM body. Same first-arg LAST keep as JSONEQ/SUBSET.
weaknesses.repro: REQUIRE JSONNEQ prev body; JSONN load FROM LAST → prev load

weaknesses.title: CHANGELOG is bag LAST not plate; arrow format quotes strings
weaknesses.detail: LAST becomes multi-line log; HAS/HASLINE for substrings. String values appear quoted in log (zone: "east" → "west"). PRINT_JSON collapses newlines (W151).
weaknesses.repro: JSONCHANGELOG; HAS log "load:" and "→"

weaknesses.title: LOADPLATE LAST_N is hit polarity (1=file, 0=fallback) not plate size
weaknesses.detail: Successful file load → LAST_N=1; miss/non-object → LAST_N=0 with defaults in LAST. Easy to confuse with empty plate (JSONEMPTY). Check LOADPLATE_HIT / FALLBACK or LAST_N==1 for hit.
weaknesses.repro: LOADPLATE miss OR defs → LAST_N 0 FALLBACK 1; plate still has keys

weaknesses.title: REQUIRE JSONTYPE fail → shell 1 exit_code 0 (W152 class)
weaknesses.detail: Wrong kind: err 'n is str, want num' (good UX) but asserts_fail path, shell 1, exit_code 0. Soft JSONTYPE + EXIT n under env for ops rc.
weaknesses.repro: REQUIRE JSONTYPE {n:"str"} n num → shell 1 exit_code 0

weaknesses.title: ok:1 is num not bool — type contracts must match encode style
weaknesses.detail: JSONOBJ ok 1 yields kind num; live true yields bool. Agents copying HTTP bool flags as 0|1 fail REQUIRE JSONTYPE ok bool. Soft probe first.
weaknesses.repro: JSONTYPE ok FROM {ok:1} → num; live true → bool

weaknesses.title: SAVEPLATE leaves LAST as path string, not plate content
weaknesses.detail: After SAVEPLATE path body, LAST is path (SAVEPLATE_PATH) and LAST_N is byte size. Chain peel JSONN FROM LAST fails. Agents must peel FROM body or LOADPLATE after save. Dual of LOADPLATE which puts content in LAST.
weaknesses.repro: SAVEPLATE p body; JSONN k FROM LAST → miss; peel FROM body or LOADPLATE p

weaknesses.title: ENSUREPLATE LAST_N polarity opposite LOADPLATE hit
weaknesses.detail: ENSURE first create LAST_N=1 CREATED=1; second load LAST_N=0 HIT=1. LOADPLATE uses LAST_N=1 for file hit. Mixing without CREATED/HIT flags confuses boot scripts.
weaknesses.repro: ENSURE miss→1 create; ENSURE again→0 load; LOADPLATE hit→1

weaknesses.title: REQUIRE PLATEFILE miss → shell 1 exit_code 0 (W152 class)
weaknesses.detail: Missing object plate: err lists path + soft twin LOADPLATE/ENSUREPLATE, asserts_fail, shell 1, exit_code 0. Soft LOADPLATE + EXIT n under env for ops rc.
weaknesses.repro: REQUIRE PLATEFILE /tmp/none.json → shell 1 exit_code 0

weaknesses.title: GETFLAGOUT path-absolutizes bare flag values
weaknesses.detail: GETFLAGOUT key|k OR … for --key=zone yields cwd/zone (path-like). Field ids must use GETFLAG/GETFLAGMS, not GETFLAGOUT. First realworld hit while wiring UPDATEPLATE --key/--val.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAGOUT key OR zone with --key=zone → /cwd/zone plate keys

weaknesses.title: UPDATEPLATE value rejects bare numeric LET vars
weaknesses.detail: SYS UPDATEPLATE path "load" take_n hard-fails need value when take_n is num. Parenthesized expr (take_n) or literal works; SYS STR stores JSON string not number. resolve_str_arg only accepts is_str idents; num branch only for TK_NUM/LPAREN.
weaknesses.repro: LET n=1; UPDATEPLATE p "load" n → need value; UPDATEPLATE p "load" (n) ok

weaknesses.title: SYS JSON does not resolve variable key names
weaknesses.detail: SYS JSON k FROM body peels literal field "k" (or miss json: no field k), not value of k. Dynamic peels need JSONPLUCK body k or fixed string keys.
weaknesses.repro: LET k zone; SYS JSON k FROM body → miss; SYS JSONPLUCK body k → east

weaknesses.title: VM var table hard-capped at 128; late LET silently fails
weaknesses.detail: Var vars[128]; n_vars>=128 → var_get create returns NULL. Agent boards with agent_boot+IDENTITY+GETFLAGOUT side-effects sit ~97 vars before work; UPDATEPLATE injects many host knobs (UPDATEPLATE_*, SAVEPLATE_*, JSONSET_*). Further LET empty="" no-ops; resolve_str_arg then hard-fails need key. Workarounds: reuse LETs, literal "" keys, lean side-effect surface.
weaknesses.repro: heavy board + 2×UPDATEPLATE then LET empty=""; UPDATEPLATE row empty 1 → need key hard

weaknesses.title: UPDATEPLATE LAST_N is insert/update not success; non-object wipe
weaknesses.detail: LAST_N=0 key-inserted / 1 key-updated (json_set n). OK=1 is success. Non-object file body silently reseeded to {} with CREATED=1 (data loss). Bool true peels as "1" via SYS JSON. No multi-key batch — gate needs N successive calls.
weaknesses.repro: WRITE junk; UPDATEPLATE k v → plate {k:v} only; true→JSON peel 1

weaknesses.title: GETFLAG rejects flag name 'or' and multi-char |aliases like fb|fallback
weaknesses.detail: GETFLAG or|fallback OR … hard-fails (OR chain keyword). GETFLAG fb|fallback also errs treating fallback as OR clause. Short single-token names (fb, key|k) work. Agents cannot name CLI flags or/fallback without workarounds.
weaknesses.repro: GETFLAG or|fallback OR ENV X OR d → parse err; GETFLAG fb OR … ok

weaknesses.title: Plate-file ops flood var table; PEEKPLATE_HIT/DROPPLATE_HIT may be missing
weaknesses.detail: Reconfirmed W174 under BUMP+PEEK+DROP: host knobs (PEEKPLATE_HIT, DROPPLATE_HIT, BUMPPLATE_CREATED) often absent after agent_boot+IDENTITY+GETFLAGOUT. Prefer LAST_N immediately after each SYS op (hit=1/0). Late LET of new names still silent-fails at 128.
weaknesses.repro: after 2 plate ops LET x = PEEKPLATE_HIT may be 0 always; use LAST_N instead

weaknesses.title: PEEKPLATE with OR returns OK=1 on miss/missing file
weaknesses.detail: Designed soft fallback: miss key or missing file with OR yields OK=1 HIT=0 LAST=fallback. Agents using OR cannot rely on OK for hard require; must branch LAST_N/HIT and EXIT n under env require.
weaknesses.repro: PEEKPLATE miss.json k OR none → OK=1; REQUIRE path needs EXIT on LAST_N==0

weaknesses.title: DROPPLATE missing file creates empty {} plate (side-effect write)
weaknesses.detail: DROPPLATE on absent path CREATED=1 writes {}. Soft miss key is OK=1 HIT=0 idempotent. Agents doing field GC must not DROP on paths they never intended to create.
weaknesses.repro: RM fresh; DROPPLATE fresh ghost → file exists JSONEMPTY 1

weaknesses.title: DECRPLATE on missing key seeds 0 then −1
weaknesses.detail: BUMP 0 + DECR on new key yields load:-1. Useful for signed counters but surprising for 'ensure then dec' budgets without prior seed.
weaknesses.repro: DECRPLATE newpath load → {"load":-1}

weaknesses.title: JSONFILEMERGE LAST_N is overlay key count not success
weaknesses.detail: LAST_N = number of keys applied from overlay (empty {} → 0). OK=1 is success. Agents must not treat LAST_N>0 as hit polarity alone when overlay is empty-by-design.
weaknesses.repro: JSONFILEMERGE path {} → OK=1 LAST_N=0 base preserved

weaknesses.title: JSONFILEMERGE create-on-miss writes nested plate from overlay only
weaknesses.detail: Missing path: mkdir parent + write overlay as plate (CREATED). No base to preserve. Useful for first-run seed overlay; dangerous if path typo silently creates.
weaknesses.repro: RM nested/fresh; JSONFILEMERGE deep {boot:1} → file exists

weaknesses.title: MERGEPLATE is in-memory only; file ops need JSONFILEMERGE/OVERLAYPLATE
weaknesses.detail: Name trap: MERGEPLATE stays JSONMERGE-on-strings. File dual is JSONFILEMERGE|OVERLAYPLATE|MERGEPLATEFILE|APPLYPLATE. Agents grepping MERGE alone may wire wrong form.
weaknesses.repro: MERGEPLATE a b does not touch disk; JSONFILEMERGE path over does

weaknesses.title: META/REPORT WRITE still omit trailing NL (reconfirm W5/W10)
weaknesses.detail: cat -A APOL_REPORT ends without $ on last line. Status bag lines intermediate $ only.
weaknesses.repro: cat -A APOL_REPORT.txt

weaknesses.title: SYS NUM parses LAST only; ignores following token as value source
weaknesses.detail: SYS NUM val_str does not parse val_str — it shuttles current LAST. Non-numeric LAST still OK=1 LAST_N=0 (W6 class). Agents that branch IF OK after NUM val_str silently treat any prior LAST; string ensure values like boot became phase:0. Fix: put value in LAST first or pass string through to JSONFILEENSURE.
weaknesses.repro: LET v boot; SYS NUM v  # parses LAST not v; OK=1 LAST_N=0

weaknesses.title: JSONFILEENSURE LAST_N is set(1)/had(0) not success
weaknesses.detail: OK=1 success; LAST_N=1 newly set, 0 key already present (no clobber). Same polarity class as UPDATEPLATE insert/update but inverted meaning from BUMP counters.
weaknesses.repro: ENSURE path retries 3 twice → first LAST_N=1 second 0 keep value

weaknesses.title: JSONFILETOGGLE LAST_N is new flag value 0|1; miss seeds 1
weaknesses.detail: Missing key → 1 (on). Truthy strings (on/true/yes?) flip to 0. LAST_N is not a hit bit — agents must not treat LAST_N==0 as failure.
weaknesses.repro: TOGGLE miss → LAST_N=1; TOGGLE again → 0; mode on → TOGGLE → 0

weaknesses.title: JSONFILEDEFAULTS dual of MERGE: fill-if-missing only
weaknesses.detail: LAST_N=keys newly set. Re-boot with same defs → LAST_N=0 live counters preserved. MERGE overwrites; DEFAULTS never clobbers — agents must pick form by intent.
weaknesses.repro: DEFAULTS retries=3; UPDATE 99; DEFAULTS again → still 99 LAST_N=0

weaknesses.title: GETP LAST_N is string length not hit bit
weaknesses.detail: After GETP "role", LAST=worker and LAST_N=6 (strlen). Numeric "4" → LAST_N=1. OR fallback "fb" → LAST_N=2. Agents must use OK / GETP_HIT / EQS for hit, never LAST_N==1 as presence. Same class as other peel strlen footguns.
weaknesses.repro: GETP role → LAST_N 6; GETP n=4 → LAST_N 1

weaknesses.title: JSONHAS is key-first: JSONHAS key [plate] not plate key
weaknesses.detail: SYS JSONHAS body "ok" probes key named body. Correct: JSONHAS "ok" body or JSONHASALL body "ok". Easy false friend after JSONHASALL plate keys order.
weaknesses.repro: JSONHAS body ok → 0; JSONHASALL body n ok → 1

weaknesses.title: plate_boot LET PLATE may silently fail at 128-var cap
weaknesses.detail: After agent_boot+IDENTITY+flags, ENSUREPLATE side-effects fill the table; LET PLATE=LAST can no-op. GETP/SETP then miss or thrash. Workarounds: verify via LOADPLATE path; lean LETs; avoid re-INCLUDE plate_save when PLATE undefined (unknown form PLATE).
weaknesses.repro: heavy board INCLUDE plate_boot; GETP may miss until LOADPLATE path check

weaknesses.title: SETP insert LAST_N=0 update=1; INCP LAST_N is new value
weaknesses.detail: SETP_N insert 0 / update 1 (opposite success polarity). INCP/BUMPP LAST_N is counter value. DECP negative ok. Confusing mix when mixing with GETP strlen LAST_N.
weaknesses.repro: SETP role worker → LAST_N 0; INCP n → LAST_N 1+

weaknesses.title: GETP key OR "" empty fallback confuses hit detection
weaknesses.detail: OR empty string makes miss path hard to distinguish from empty values; prefer OR "fb" sentinel or two-step GETP then GETP OR.
weaknesses.repro: GETP role OR "" after SETP may report miss LAST_N 0
